items.title: Jev: A New AI Model for Fast, Cheap Binary Decisions
points: Jev, a new AI model from TypeSafe, makes binary software decisions (yes/no style choices) 200x faster and 400x cheaper than frontier large language models (LLMs, the big general-purpose AI models like GPT-4), enabling automation of tasks like PR (pull request, a proposed code change) reviews and support ticket triage.

Claude Code can use Jev to intelligently compact coding sessions by scoring which tool calls still matter, shrinking a 1M-token session (tokens are chunks of text an AI processes) to 86K tokens in one second without losing critical context.

Browser agents powered by Jev complete tasks like flight searches in 7 seconds for under a penny by having Jev pick clicks from a numbered menu of page elements instead of an LLM analyzing screenshots.
Setup: create a free API key at console.typesafe.ai (no waitlist), export it as TYPESAFE_API_KEY, then install TypeSafe's Claude Code plugin to build a custom document-scoring tool.

Compaction workflow: install the fast-jev-compaction plugin, enable function hooks in Claude Code settings, then run /compact to prune stale tool-call results while preserving essential context like coding rules.

Browser agent workflow: install Chrome, the Python tool 'uv', and an OpenRouter account (provides a small text-only backup model), then clone the jev-ultrafast repo and run 'uv run jev' to launch an agent that completed a Zürich-to-London flight search in 7.1 seconds for $0.0039.

items.title: OpenAI Agents Leaked 53 User Images Online
points: OpenAI's AI agents leaked 53 user images online after they ended up in training data (the dataset used to teach an AI model).
The company is working with hosting providers to remove the images but declined to explain how it identified affected users.

items.title: Tesla's Optimus Robot Production Ramping Up but Bottlenecked
points: Production increased roughly tenfold, from a few dozen to hundreds of robots per week, but hand assembly and supplier limits are blocking Tesla's goal of 1,000 units weekly by year's end.
Optimus V3, built in Fremont with a lighter frame and better cameras, currently handles only narrow, supervised tasks.
Tesla plans to lease commercial robots to warehouses rather than sell them, likely starting in 2027, with robot hand design/assembly remaining a top technical hurdle.

items.title: Pentagon's Claude Ban Upheld by Federal Appeals Court
points: A Washington D.C. federal appeals court ruled 2-1 that the Defense Department had solid grounds to treat Anthropic's Claude models as a national security risk.

The ban stems from Anthropic's refusal to drop rules blocking Claude from enabling mass surveillance of Americans and autonomous weapons; Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth blocked the models for staff and contractors in June.
The ruling conflicts with an August California district court decision that called the ban illegal under a different law; Anthropic is weighing options, including a potential Supreme Court appeal.

items.title: DeepMind Engineer Quits Over AI Safety Concerns
points: Robert O'Callahan, a technical expert at Google DeepMind in New Zealand, resigned citing AI risks, saying the 'current rate of change is far too high.'

He built chip design tools that made AI cheaper and faster before quitting, and lists dangers including cognitive surrender, AI-induced psychosis, loneliness, concentrated power, and economic disruption.
He says many DeepMind colleagues privately share his safety concerns but rarely speak up publicly, and he now seeks 'unambiguously pro-human' work.

items.title: Tesla Launches Electric Semi Truck Production
points: Tesla began high-volume production of its electric Semi at a Sparks, Nevada facility, with Standard Range rated at 325 miles and Long Range at 500 miles under an 82,000-pound load.

The truck uses Tesla's 4680 battery cells (larger cylindrical cells for higher energy density) with an 822 kWh pack, and Megacharger stations (1.2 megawatts) charge trucks from 3% to 60% in about 30 minutes.
The factory can eventually produce 50,000 trucks per year, with the first vehicles already reaching customers after years of delays.
Separately, Microsoft and Qualcomm have quietly dropped the 'Copilot+ PC' branding after consumer pushback.

issues.subject: 🤖 A developer's guide to start using Jev

headlines: Jev, a new AI model from TypeSafe, makes binary software decisions 200x faster and 400x cheaper than frontier LLMs, enabling practical automation of tasks like PR reviews and support ticket triage.
Claude Code can now use Jev to intelligently compact coding sessions by scoring which tool calls still matter, reducing a 1M-token session to 86K in one second without losing critical context.
Browser agents powered by Jev complete tasks like flight searches in 7 seconds for under a penny by having Jev select clicks from a numbered menu instead of processing screenshots with an LLM.

sections.title: Setting Up Jev with Claude Code
points: 1. Create an API key at console.typesafe.ai (no waitlist), export it as TYPESAFE_API_KEY in your shell.
2. Install TypeSafe's skill plugin and start Claude Code with a prompt asking it to build a CLI for evaluating documents you choose.
3. Claude Code will ask what documents to evaluate (PRs, tickets, etc.) and what dimensions matter, then generates a tool that scores each document through Jev in milliseconds.

sections.title: Workflow #1: Intelligent Context Compaction
points: 1. Install the fast-jev-compaction plugin and enable function hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json.
2. Run /compact in a long Claude Code session; Jev scores each tool call to identify stale results worth dropping.
3. System prunes irrelevant calls without rewriting anything, preserving critical context like coding rules you've set.
4. One test reduced a session from 1M tokens to 86K in about one second while keeping all essential information.

sections.title: Workflow #2: Fast Browser Agents
points: 1. Install Chrome, the Python tool 'uv', and get an OpenRouter account (which provides the small text-only model).
2. Clone the jev-ultrafast repository and set up .env with your TypeSafe and OpenRouter API keys.
3. Run 'uv run jev' to start the agent with a local control panel; Jev selects numbered clickable elements on each page instead of processing full screenshots.
4. A test completed a Zürich-to-London flight search on Google Flights in 7.1 seconds for $0.0039, with only a small LLM waking up when typing is needed.
